correctness.rationale: For integral homogeneous binary F,G with nonzero homogeneous resultant R, modulo every p not dividing R there is no common nonzero affine zero: otherwise it would be a common projective root. Thus simultaneous p divisibility for a primitive integer coordinate pair occurs only at primes dividing R. Homogeneity also forces all value pairs from nonprimitive coordinates to share their coordinate prime. CRT gives beta=prod_{p|R}(1-N_p/p^2), with B(Y)=beta Y^2+O_{F,G}(Y+1) for local exclusions. Mobius inversion restricted to d coprime to rad(R) yields main constant beta prod_{p not |R}(1-p^-2) and O_{F,G}(X log X) via harmonic errors. Checked F=X^2-Y^2,G=X^2-4Y^2 at p3 N3=5, and F=X^2+Y^2,G=X^2-Y^2 at p2 N2=2; an independent exact pointwise grid count at N=11,29,37 matched the local/primitive condition for both. The finite checks corroborate but do not prove the universal resultant argument.
